items.label: Plan how you will disclose AI use
items.what: Plan how you will disclose AI use in publications, presentations, and to participants.
items.why: Most journals and conferences now require AI disclosure. Transparency builds trust and is increasingly required by publishers.
items.how: Draft a disclosure statement describing which AI tools were used and for what purpose. Include in your methods section.

items.label: Check AI grades for fairness
items.what: Verify AI grading produces equitable outcomes across student demographics.
items.why: AI grading tools can carry biases from training data, leading to unfair outcomes for certain student groups.
items.how: Compare AI-generated grades across demographic subgroups. Check for statistically significant disparities. Document findings and any corrections made.

items.label: Check whether FERPA applies to this data
items.what: Confirm student records processed by AI are handled per FERPA requirements.
items.why: Student education records are protected under FERPA. Sending them to external AI services may violate federal law.
items.how: Check that AI processing happens on institution-approved systems. Check vendor data processing agreements. Confirm no student data is retained by third-party AI services.

items.label: Share grading criteria with students
items.what: Ensure students are informed that AI is used in the grading process.
items.why: Students have a right to know how their work is evaluated. Transparency builds trust and meets institutional policy requirements.
items.how: Update your syllabus to include AI grading disclosure. Communicate in class and provide an opt-out or appeal mechanism if required by policy.

items.label: Decide how you will override AI grades
items.what: Define a process for students to appeal or request human review of AI-assisted grades.
items.why: Students must have recourse when they believe an AI grade is incorrect. This is both an ethical and often institutional requirement.
items.how: Establish a clear appeal window (e.g., 7 days). Document the process in the syllabus. Ensure a human instructor reviews all appeals.

items.label: Spot-check AI grades against your own
items.what: Sample and validate AI-generated grades against instructor judgment.
items.why: AI grading must be verified for accuracy before being applied at scale. Unvalidated AI grades risk harming student outcomes.
items.how: Review a random 20-25% sample of AI grades. Compare with your own assessment. Document agreement rate and any adjustments made.

items.label: Check that the data is de-identified
items.what: Ensure personal identifiers are removed before AI processing.
items.why: Sending identifiable data to AI systems (especially cloud-based) may violate privacy regulations and IRB requirements.
items.how: Remove or mask: names, dates, locations, ID numbers, photos, and any combination that could identify someone. Use established de-identification standards (HIPAA Safe Harbor or Expert Determination).

items.label: Confirm your IRB protocol covers AI use
items.what: Verify whether your research requires IRB approval and if your current protocol covers AI use.
items.why: IRB approval obtained before AI tools existed may not cover new AI methods. Using AI on human subjects data without IRB approval that covers it can violate your protocol.
items.how: Check your IRB protocol. If AI is not mentioned, contact your IRB office to determine if an amendment is needed.

items.label: Classify the data you will use
items.what: Identify what type of data you are using and its sensitivity level.
items.why: Different data types have different handling requirements. Identifiable health data requires stricter controls than public datasets.
items.how: Categorize your data: Public, Internal, Confidential, or Restricted. Check if it contains PII, PHI, or other sensitive information.

items.label: Confirm where data and AI outputs are stored
items.what: Verify that data and AI outputs are stored securely.
items.why: Research data requires protection from unauthorized access. Cloud AI services may retain data unless configured otherwise.
items.how: Use institutional approved storage. Check AI service data retention policies. Enable encryption at rest and in transit.

items.label: Disclose AI-assisted coding
items.what: Document how AI was used in qualitative coding or analysis.
items.why: Using AI to code interviews or analyze text changes the methodology. Reviewers and readers need to evaluate this.
items.how: Describe the AI tool used, what it did (initial codes, theme suggestions), and how human researchers validated or modified the output.

items.label: Check that participant consent covers AI use
items.what: Ensure consent forms mention AI processing of participant data.
items.why: Participants have a right to know their data will be processed by AI systems, especially if using cloud-based tools.
items.how: Review consent forms. If AI use was not mentioned, consult IRB about whether re-consent or notification is needed.

items.label: Assess how AI affects decisions about people
items.what: Document who is affected by AI-assisted administrative decisions and how.
items.why: Administrative decisions (admissions, resource allocation, scheduling) carry high-stakes consequences for individuals and groups.
items.how: Identify all stakeholders affected. Estimate the number of people impacted. Assess potential consequences of incorrect decisions. Document findings.

items.label: Define how people can appeal a decision
items.what: Ensure individuals affected by AI-informed decisions can challenge them.
items.why: People affected by automated decisions have a right to human review. This is both an ethical obligation and increasingly a legal requirement.
items.how: Create a written appeal process with clear timelines. Ensure a human decision-maker reviews all appeals. Publish the process where affected parties can find it.

items.label: Check administrative decisions for bias
items.what: Test for disparate impact on protected groups in AI-assisted decisions.
items.why: AI systems can perpetuate or amplify existing institutional biases, leading to discrimination in administrative outcomes.
items.how: Analyze decision outcomes across demographic groups. Use disparate impact ratio (4/5ths rule) to identify potential bias. Document findings and corrective actions.

items.label: Use only the data you need
items.what: Confirm only necessary data is used in administrative AI processing.
items.why: Using excessive personal data increases privacy risk and potential for misuse without improving decision quality.
items.how: Audit which data fields the AI system uses. Remove any fields not essential to the decision. Document the rationale for each retained field.

items.label: Tell affected people how AI is used
items.what: Notify people affected by decisions that AI was involved in the process.
items.why: Transparency about AI involvement in decisions builds trust and is increasingly required by institutional policy and regulation.
items.how: Include AI disclosure in decision notification letters/emails. Add disclosure to relevant web pages and application forms. Make the disclosure clear and prominent.

items.label: Decide how a person reviews AI output
items.what: Establish how humans will review and validate AI outputs.
items.why: AI systems make errors. Human oversight catches mistakes and maintains accountability, especially for consequential decisions.
items.how: Define: Who reviews AI outputs? What percentage is reviewed? What are the criteria for acceptance/rejection? Document the review process.
